name: ipad-tcg
accel_note: Intel Windows host: TCG is mandatory. The launcher refuses any other accelerator (accelerator_not_tcg).
cpu_model_note: Pinned to the board we boot: run-qemu.py:155 selects cortex-a710 for TCG, and the ADT's cpu0 compatible is arm,cortex-a710 (make-dt.py:141). The earlier cortex-a57 guess was ARMv8.0 and is superseded.
memory_note: board.toml:92 dram_size = 0x180000000 (6 GiB); make-qemu-adt.py is called with --dram-size 0x180000000, so a smaller guest would describe memory the ADT says does not exist. Host has 15.8GB total.
machine_type_note: run-qemu.py:154. virtualization=off because TCG is not a virtualizer; secure=off because there is no TrustZone; gic-version=3 because board.toml describes GICv3.

resolution_catalogue.name: ramfb-pinned
resolution_catalogue.provenance: Pinned board geometry: this file's display and run-qemu.py:39-43. The real 1366-wide panel rounded up to the 16-pixel width multiple. This is the geometry this project boots.

resolution_catalogue.name: ipad-4-3-standard
resolution_catalogue.provenance: 4:3 iPad-class reference panel (2048x1536). Already a multiple of 16 on both axes, so the framebuffer constraint needs no rounding.

resolution_catalogue.name: ipad-pro-12-9
resolution_catalogue.provenance: iPad Pro 12.9-inch reference panel (2732x2048) rounded up: 2732 is not a multiple of 16, the framebuffer width is 2736.

resolution_catalogue.name: ipad-pro-11
resolution_catalogue.provenance: iPad Pro 11-inch reference panel (2388x1668) rounded up on both axes to 2400x1680.

resolution_catalogue.name: ipad-mini-8-3
resolution_catalogue.provenance: iPad mini (8.3-inch) reference panel (2266x1488) rounded up: 2266 is not a multiple of 16, the framebuffer width is 2288.

display.resolution_catalogue_note: The five geometries the launcher accepts, listed here so an operator can choose one without reading src/. Exactly one entry carries pinned: true -- the geometry this project boots. The other four are iPad-class reference panel sizes offered so an operator can ASK for a different framebuffer; their panel dimensions are published device specifications, not measurements from this host, and no resolution other than the pinned one has been shown to render on a real iPadOS guest. Whether the guest renders correctly at one is a field question this configuration cannot answer. Editing this list does NOT add a resolution: unipad.host.display.DISPLAY_MODES is the enforcer and must be changed too, or the launcher refuses the pair with config_invalid rather than accepting it. This list is the readable surface, not the validator, and tests/unit/test_host_display_route.py fails if the two ever disagree.
display.note: ramfb/GOP path first (PRD 4.2); VirtIO GPU software path probed at M9a. Geometry is run-qemu.py:39-43 and reaches the guest driver via fw_cfg opt/org.unixnu/ramfb-size -- width must be a multiple of 16 and rows a multiple of 64 bytes, which the real 1366-wide panel is not.
display.resolution_note: PRD 3.2 P1 (4). One of the five catalogue geometries listed in resolution_catalogue above; a pair outside that catalogue is REFUSED with config_invalid, never snapped to a neighbour, because a framebuffer that is not the one asked for makes the recorded geometry disagree with the pixels in the screenshot. Only the pinned entry is a geometry this project boots. On the virtio-gpu route the resolution does NOT reach the guest: that route negotiates its own geometry (ADR-0004) and emits no fw_cfg item, so the request is validated, recorded and then dropped. This is the same limitation rotation_note describes, stated for resolution because the two used to be documented asymmetrically. The drop has a closed machine-readable vocabulary -- DisplayDecision.route_limitations, key resolution_not_configured -- and it is unit-pinned in tests/unit/test_host_display_route.py. It is NOT yet in any evidence bundle, and this note will not claim otherwise: no run path calls DisplayDecision.to_dict(), and cmd_start builds launch.json from LaunchResult.to_dict(), which carries no display block. The only current trace of the drop is the absence of the -fw_cfg item in the argv. Naming the gap here rather than promising the evidence is deliberate -- a promise nothing keeps is the same defect this note was written to correct.
display.rotation_note: PRD 3.2 P1 (4). Quarter turn in degrees, one of 0/90/180/270; 0 is the board orientation. Rotation is applied to the framebuffer, so the fw_cfg item carries the rotated geometry. On the virtio-gpu route rotation does NOT reach the guest -- that route negotiates its own geometry (ADR-0004).
display.audio_note: PRD 3.2 P1 (4). 'none' emits no audio device; 'hda' emits intel-hda with a null host driver, so a guest driver has something to bind to while no host sound hardware is opened. Guest audio has never been heard on this host and no configuration here can claim otherwise.

firmware.note: UEFI variables live in a writable second flash device; -bios cannot express that and the two spellings are mutually exclusive in qemu-virt.c:1907-1916. vars.fd is created per run at the code drive's size (67108864 here).

data_disk.note: Persistent Data volume; route decided by H04 (M9b)

input.note: Text input may start on the guest on-screen keyboard (FR04)

net.note: M13; disabled for MVP boot gates
net.enabled_note: PRD 3.2 P1 (1). Enabling it turns on QEMU's user-mode (SLIRP) stack with restrict=on by default, which is loopback-only: the guest can reach the host's package service at 10.0.2.2 and cannot reach the public internet. Setting restrict=off is the one change that gives the guest public egress and needs explicit operator authorisation. Two further conditions, because a reader who misses either gets a refusal or a silent no-op rather than the network described above: (a) enabling the device is NOT sufficient on its own -- a mode key is REQUIRED, and an enabled flag alone is refused with config_invalid 'mode is required when the network is enabled'; (b) the package service at 10.0.2.2 exists only on the install/update --transport https route -- the default transport is channel, which starts no service (ADR-0008), so with the default an enabled network reaches no package.
net.host_forwards_note: PRD 3.2 P1 (1). One object per rule: {"host_port": 9443, "guest_port": 8443} emits hostfwd=tcp:127.0.0.1:9443-10.0.2.15:8443. hostfwd maps a HOST port INTO the guest; it is not how the package service is reached (the guest connects out to 10.0.2.2, which needs no -nic change). Empty by default, so no mapping is opened that nobody asked for.

control.note: QMP over Windows socket; serial and control must not contend

disks.artifact_root_note: C: has 0.6GB free; never place images there.
